Synopsis:
Brazil's July current account deficit hit $8.11B, a 7-year high for the month, significantly missing the $6.6B forecast. Deterioration was broad-based: services deficit +$500M YoY, factor payments -$400M, trade surplus -$200M. FDI came in at $7.46B, below the $7.92B forecast and down from $8.4B a year prior. On a rolling 12-month basis, FDI (3.50% of GDP) still covers the current account deficit (2.49% of GDP), but both metrics are trending in the wrong direction, applying downward pressure on the Brazilian Real (BRL).
